sections.category: Agent harness: Databricks open-sources Omnigent, a meta-harness that wraps Claude Code, Codex and agent SDKs behind one interface

bullets.body: Databricks introduced Omnigent on June 13, an open-source (Apache 2.0, alpha) meta-harness that sits a layer above individual coding agents and agent SDKs so a developer can drive several of them through one common interface instead of juggling separate tools. It targets composition, control and collaboration: a shared interface over command-line agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) and SDKs (OpenAI Agents, Claude Agents SDK) so implementations can be swapped without rewriting; stateful, contextual policies enforced at the meta-harness layer that track agent actions and apply guardrails such as cost budgets, permissions and OS-level sandboxing; and live agent sessions that can be shared by URL so teammates review files, comment and steer the same run together. Sessions reach across web, mobile, a macOS app and APIs, with cloud execution on Modal and Daytona sandboxes and multi-harness agents authored in YAML. The release lands alongside the Data + AI Summit but is published as a standalone OSS project on GitHub rather than a Databricks-only feature.

citations.label: Databricks Blog - Introducing Omnigent: A Meta-Harness to Combine, Control and Share Your Agents

sections.category: Local LLM optimization research: a cached-rollout RL recipe trains small tool-calling agents toward frontier accuracy at a fraction of the compute

bullets.body: A June 12 arXiv paper, CacheRL: Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents via Cached Rollouts and Hybrid Reward (arXiv:2606.14179), tackles a practical bottleneck in fine-tuning small agent models: doing reinforcement learning on multi-turn tool use normally requires expensive live tool execution. CacheRL instead replays a three-tier fuzzy cache of trajectories with token-level masking to avoid live calls, and pairs it with a cache-tier-aware hybrid reward that dynamically reweights answer quality so the model is not penalized for limitations the cache itself introduces. The authors report 92% process accuracy on multi-step tool-calling tasks, approaching GPT-5's reported 94% while using roughly 100x less compute, and lift validation reward on Qwen3-4B-Thinking from 0.43 to 0.78; ablations attribute a 41% drop to removing knowledge transfer and a 17% gain to the cache-aware reward. The result is a concrete recipe for distilling tool-calling competence into a small open model without a costly live-execution RL loop.

citations.label: arXiv - CacheRL: Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents via Cached Rollouts and Hybrid Reward

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: the Databricks Data + AI Summit opens Monday at Moscone, anchoring a summer calendar across dev/data, AI-security and AI-chip tracks

bullets.body: The still-upcoming calendar worth planning attendance around spans three tracks, with this week's live anchor being the mainstream dev/data event. Mainstream dev/data: the Databricks Data + AI Summit opens today and runs June 15-18 across Moscone in San Francisco (30,000-plus in person from 150-plus countries; keynotes from co-founders Ali Ghodsi, Matei Zaharia, Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji and Reynold Xin, plus OpenAI's Greg Brockman, a recorded Satya Nadella fireside and a multi-day hackathon with OpenAI), and the AI Engineer World's Fair follows June 29-July 2 at Moscone West with dedicated Inference and Security tracks. AI-security: the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, on confidential agents and secure AI workflows); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay; in Las Vegas, Black Hat USA's AI Summit sits inside the August 1-6 conference at Mandalay Bay alongside DEF CON's AI Village; OWASP Global AppSec USA runs November 5-6 in San Francisco; and Zenity's practitioner-led AI Agent Security Summit, which the user tracks, has a 2026 global series with New York, London and APAC dates still to be announced. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is locked to July 23 at Moscone (Instinct/MI400-series focus expected); Hot Chips 2026 takes Stanford's Memorial Auditorium August 23-25; and the AI Infra Summit runs September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center (8,000-plus attendees across compute, AI data centers and physical AI). Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas.
